utterances.text: This document refers to the assignment of soldiers from the 328th Mountain Brigade, 12 from each of the battalions, and their attachment to the El Mujahid unit. They were mostly used to carry the wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, perhaps, in the English version, we could go to the top of the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you see the reference to your battalion, sir, on this document?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, the 5th Battalion of the 328th Brigade, ten men.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And what was the purpose, as you've told us this document refers to the assignment of soldiers from the 328th and their attachment to the El Mujahid unit, what was the purpose for subordinating soldiers to the El Mujahid unit?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The El Mujahid Detachment did not number a lot of soldiers at the time, so they used our soldiers in order to carry out the wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, objection. The phrase used earlier by the witness was "attachment," and in the last question by the Prosecutor, it was asked: "What was the purpose for subordinating soldiers to the El Mujahid unit?" So it was a leading question, suggesting that this was subordination. In our submission, there's a difference between "detachment" -- or there could be a difference between "detachment" and "subordination."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: There could be a difference between?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: "Detachment" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: "Detachment" or "attachment."

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm trying to find the exact expression used by the witness. I believe it was "attachment."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's right. Okay. Mr. Mundis, do you follow the drift?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I do, but I think it's a distinction without a difference, but I'll rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell the Trial Chamber why men were attached from the 5th Battalion of the 328th Brigade to the El Mujahid unit?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The El Mujahid unit used the soldiers from the 5th Battalion, i.e., from the 328th Brigade, to carry the fallen and wounded soldiers, which is exactly what is stated in the document. Usually, one of the commanders would go together with our soldiers, which means that those soldiers were not under the command of the El Mujahid unit. They were just assigned to them to assist them with some tasks, such as the carrying of the wounded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could we go to the previous page, please. Can we go to the previous page on this document, both. I want the witness -- well, stay on the same page in B/C/S. Sir, I would like to understand something, and you may be able to explain it to us by reading the B/C/S version. It says here, if you look at the 3rd and 4th Battalions: "11 fighters, plus 15 carriers of the wounded." So it seems as if, from the 3rd Battalion, not only are we getting carriers of the wounded, but we are also getting fighters. Eleven of them are fighters and 15 of them are carriers, so it doesn't look to me as if the battalions were being assigned to the El Mujahid Detachment for purposes of carrying the wounded only, but also for fighting. Am I wrong in that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the El Mujahid unit did not trust the soldiers that manned the defence line, and it would only very rarely use them in combat because they did not have enough experience. Sometimes they would use them if the conflict was a smaller-scale one. They mostly used them to carry their wounded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Would this be one of those rare occasions where they used them also for combat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Prosecution moves this document into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 699.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: May the witness now be shown PT2096, PT2096.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you see this document, sir?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber what this document is, please?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is an order by the commander of the 328th Mountain Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And can we focus your attention, sir, on paragraph 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And for that purpose, we need to go to page 2 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, again, sir, in the middle of paragraph 3, again, we see some numbers indicated. Can you tell the Trial Chamber what this document relates to, in terms of these numbers?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Again, this is an order by which ten fighters and 30 carriers of the wounded are assigned from the 5th Battalion for the execution of a certain task.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We would tender this document into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 700.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I note the time, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you saying you it is --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: It would be convenient, Your Honour. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. I thought you were saying you just noted it, but you were still doing something else. Thank you very much. We'll take an adjournment and come back at half past 12.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can the witness now be shown PT2103, please. PT2103.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Sehic, can you tell us what this document is, please?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think this is a report of the brigade commander to the commander of the 35th Division.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you please --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If we could scroll down in the Bosnian version to the very bottom of the document, and in the English, if we could go to page 3 in the middle, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Sehic, do you see the very bottom paragraph of this document?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us what that refers to, please?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: "Raising the unit's readiness to full combat readiness, with certain tasks. Take 12 soldiers out of the reconnaissance unit and 30 helpers to carry the wounded, and leave them in the deployment area of the village of Sehici."

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, can you tell us or tell the Trial Chamber the reference to the 30 carriers for the wounded, what other unit, if any, were these 30 carriers for the wounded deployed with?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In the vicinity of the 4th Manoeuvre Battalion or other battalions of the 328th Brigade, that's where they were probably deployed. That's the area of Sehici. At least this order states that they should be on standby.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We would ask that this document be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 701.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can the witness now be shown PT2104, please. PT2104.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document, sir?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us what this document is, please?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is the implementation of the earlier order of the brigade commander, whereby these 30 soldiers were detached from their units to carry out the task of carrying the wounded. The commanding officers who were supposed to be in charge of the 30 men were also designated in this order. At the point in time when the superior command decides to issue such an order, they would be subordinated to the El Mujahid unit -- resubordinated to the El Mujahid unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If you could please focus your attention on paragraph 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And if we could go to the next page in the English translation, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us what the meaning of paragraph 4 is?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This means that together with the El Mujahid unit, they would be assigned to a given task. Here, this relates to the 30 men assigned to carry the wounded; and, probably, at the certain point in time, they would do precisely that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And who signed this document, sir?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I personally did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We would ask that this document be admitted into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 702.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can the witness now be shown PT2124, PT2124.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Again, Mr. Sehic, I'd ask you if you recognise this document.

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Who signed this document?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you please look at the first paragraph of this document. Take a look at that, and I'd like to ask you some questions about that.

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you describe or recall -- if you recall, tell the Trial Chamber what this paragraph relates to, please.

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Out of every company, ten soldiers were supposed to be assigned to keep the defence lines reached. That meant the total of 30 men.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you comment, sir, upon the phrase "with the El Mujahid unit" at the end of that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The El Mujahid unit had liberated the Podsjelovo feature in offensive activities; and, as this was a rather large area, they were unable to hold it themselves. They, therefore, sought assistance from the 328th Brigade, or rather, its battalions, who then reassigned some men out of their units to hold the newly-reached lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The Prosecution asks that this document be admitted into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 703.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We would ask the witness now be shown PT2130, PT2130, and if we could please go to about --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me ask you this, sir: Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'll will withdraw this document. Let's now show the witness PT2162, PT2162.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document, sir?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. This is my document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you turn your attention, please, to paragraph 2 of this document. I'd like to ask if you could perhaps elaborate or comment upon paragraph 2 of this order.

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was necessary to select ten most highly-skilled servicemen for combat activities from each platoon, probably because they were preparing for certain combat actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall, sir, what combat actions?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I believe that they were due to liberate the Podsjelovo feature. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders this document into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 704.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We would now ask the witness be shown PT2323, PT2323.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document, sir?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Who signed this document?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I signed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you please look at paragraph (a) of this document.

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you comment upon what's being ordered in this document of yours, sir?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: These are soldiers who had been attached to the El Mujahid unit earlier on and were probably about to be attached to them again, in order to carry out certain combat tasks on a given date; that is to say, the 26th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. The Prosecution tenders this document into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Prosecutor. Could we elicit from the witness how the soldiers that were allocated or subordinated to the EMD for these particular actions, how were they taken back to the 2nd Company?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Sehic, do you understand the question Judge Harhoff has asked you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Did you issue a new order to have them assigned back to you each time, or did they just come back automatically after having completed the actions for which they were assigned to the EMD?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They would come back of their own accord once they completed their assignments. We did not write orders to that effect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you tender it, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We do tender it, yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. It is admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 705.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Sehic, I'd like to turn to one final topic to discuss with you, and that concerns training. Can you tell the Trial Chamber where the 5th Battalion of the 328th Mountain Brigade conducted or underwent training in 1995?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Training was normally held in the general area of Gostovici, in the hamlet of Sehici, from where most of the soldiers in question hailed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And when you say, sir, "in the area of Gostovici," can you tell the Trial Chamber in what location or locations this training was held?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: For the most part, in the fields in the vicinity of the school building or close to the logistics or rear command post of the 5th Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And who conducted the training which you've referred to in the vicinity of the school?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Normally, platoon commanders and some of the senior commanding officers of the El Mujahid unit when it came to religious training. It depended on what kind of training it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you describe for the Trial Chamber a little bit about this training which you've referred to by the officers of the El Mujahid unit?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did not attend their training, and I cannot give you the details of it. Generally speaking, the soldiers, as they came back from that training, would complain about the El Mujahid officers having been hard upon their heels, asking them to work. It was mostly religious training, and some of it was dedicated to them being physically fit, in order to be able to carry the wounded and pull the dead out of a combat area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, with respect to soldiers of the 5th Battalion of the 328th Mountain Brigade who underwent this training from the El Mujahid unit officers, can you describe for us how that came about, in terms of how people were selected or sent for this training?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Platoon commanders or company commanders did the selecting. I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: How long would this training last?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: A couple of days, two to three days, depending on how much spare time the soldiers had. Normally, they didn't have much spare time because they were duty-bound to be on the defence line. One unit would be manning the defence line, one would be on standby, and a third one would be resting. So they could not have lasted more than a day or two.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Sehic. The Prosecution has no further questions at this time, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Mundis. Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: If you'll just bear with me a moment, please, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Sehic. I'll be asking you some questions today on behalf of General Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Can you confirm, Mr. Sehic, that before joining the ARBiH, you had little or no military experience?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Next to none.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: You certainly hadn't served in a position as a commander of an army unit?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I hadn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And before the war, it's correct to say that you worked as a metalworker?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, you told us that after holding various positions in the ARBiH, it was in March or April of 1995 that you became the commander of the 5th Battalion of the 328th Brigade; is that so?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And during 1995, your headquarters was in the village of Marici, and you had a rear command post in the village of Borovnica, specifically in the hamlet of Sehici?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, the Prosecution has just shown you a number of documents in which the El Mujahid unit is mentioned. It's correct, isn't it, that during 1995, the El Mujahedin Detachment performed reconnaissance at the front line where your battalion operated?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And is it correct to say that on a number of occasions, the El Mujahedin Detachment would pass through your battalion's area of responsibility without making any announcement?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, they mostly never announced that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Normally, if one army unit is passing through the area of responsibility of another unit, the commander of that unit would expect to receive some sort of communication about the movement; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And it's right that problems can arise if you have one unit passing through the unit of another without any sort of communication or announcement?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, yes. For the most part, there were problems with the El Mujahid unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So the El Mujahedin Detachment didn't communicate to you when they were passing through your area of responsibility. It's right to say that you could do nothing about that?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: If I can ask you about the appearance of these members of the El Mujahedin Detachment that came into your area of responsibility. Would you agree with me that some of them wore military uniforms; whereas, others wore civilian clothing or non-military clothing?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The El Mujahid passing through my area of responsibility had some sort of uniform, most of them. But they did not have any insignia, and we believed them all to be or to have been members of the El Mujahid unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: The Prosecution showed you a document a little earlier about El Mujahedin -- the El Mujahedin Detachment in your AOR.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: If we could please bring up Exhibit 698, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Sehic, do you recall being shown this document earlier today?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: You were asked about paragraph 3 of the document, which states: "By 1200 hours on the 14th of April, 1995, take the Rudine defence line which had been taken by the El Mujahedin unit." Now, is it right to say, Mr. Sehic, that the reason you had to issue this order was because earlier that day, the El Mujahedin Detachment had simply got up and left the front line at about 9.00 in the morning?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. In the morning, perhaps even earlier than 9.00, they left the line of their own accord without even letting us know about it. It was the soldiers who were close to those positions that told us about it, and I then issued an order assigning these men to occupy that line.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So they left the line of their own accord. Was the result of the El Mujahedin Detachment doing that a danger or risk that the enemy forces would simply be able to come down and take the unmanned line -- front line?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So you had to act quickly to ensure that the front line was still kept under the control of the ARBiH?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. I reported to the brigade commander about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: In your statement, the statement that you gave to the Office of the Prosecution investigator, at paragraph 36, you said that the El Mujahedin Detachment came into your area of responsibility and did whatever they wished. Do you stand by that comment in your statement?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Sehic, I'd like to turn to the documents that you were shown concerning the attachment of soldiers from your unit to the El Mujahedin Detachment. Now, earlier on in your evidence, you told us that those men were used to carry the wounded and fallen soldiers. It's right to say, isn't it, that when the men from your battalion were attached to the El Mujahedin Detachment, you defined the tasks and duties that they had to carry out?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Next to a number of soldiers, every -- almost every order also designates a commanding officer who was in charge of men, and their task was only to occupy the defence lines reached and to take care of the wounded. The orders would be issued by the commanding officers in charge of such groups of men.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So it's correct to say that at no time were those soldiers placed under the command of the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Not directly, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Could we describe this as being a case of coordination between your unit and the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The battalion level did not have any particular coordination with the El Mujahid unit; however, we were duty-bound to designate a commanding officer to accompany every group of men and who was responsible for the soldiers from the 5th Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So perhaps, Mr. Sehic, just to clarify that, we could describe this more as a case of cooperation between the two units?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: I'd just like to refer to some of the documents that you were shown.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: If we could bring up Exhibit 700, please. And in this document, it's page 2 of the English version that I'm interested in. Perhaps if we can look at the first page to establish what the document is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document from a little earlier, Mr. Sehic?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The brigade commander issued this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Yes. I'm interested in point number 3, which you were asked to comment upon by the Prosecutor. If I could just read out what this paragraph states, it says: "By 1200 hours on 24 May 1995, place the units for carrying out the combat tasks on full combat readiness and billet them in barracks or buildings under full combat gear and with numerical strength according to the following disposition." And then we can see, Mr. Sehic, in respect of the five battalions, it gives some instructions about the soldiers of those battalions. Do you accept that?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, if we can just look at the first one, by way of example, it states here: "1st Mountain Battalion, 12 soldiers for BZ," which I take to mean "combat tasks," "and 30 bearers for the wounded for the El Mujahid." Would you agree with me, Mr. Sehic, that what the brigade commander is doing in this order is placing 12 soldiers from the 1st Battalion on combat readiness, and then separately he is instructing 30 soldiers to carry out duties as bearers for the wounded from the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I've already stated that soldiers who were assigned for combat activities would take the lines reached. They were mostly not used for combat. And as for those who were assigned to bear the wounded, their tasks were quite well defined.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So just to clarify that, what I'm trying to get at, from this order, is that the 12 soldiers from the 1st Mountain Battalion who were tasked for combat readiness, they are not being tasked to cooperate or work alongside the El Mujahedin Detachment, are they?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. No battalion was given any precise assignment to that effect, i.e., the assignment for the ten men from the battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Okay. Now, we can see that the date of this document is the 23rd of May, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: I'd now like to turn to Exhibit 701, which is dated the 24th of May, 1995 -- I beg your pardon, it should be Exhibit 702.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So, Mr. Sehic, would you agree with me that in the last document that we just looked at a moment ago, that was the order of the brigade commander; and what we can see in front of us now, dated the 24th of May, 1995, this is your instructions to your subordinates based on that order?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And, then, it's clear here, in this order at point number 1, that you are ordering 30 men to be selected to carry the wounded, and that was in accordance with the order of Commander Zilkic?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honours, we can put this document away. I'd like to, still on this topic, turn now to Exhibit 703.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, while we're waiting for the document to come up: Mr. Sehic, you told us in your evidence a little earlier on that when men were attached to the El Mujahedin Detachment, they would have their own commander?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I believe that every statement that I ever issued indicates the person responsible, sometimes even by name. It would have been the platoon or company commander. It would state clearly that that person was responsible for the execution of a certain task.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And just to confirm that point, this is a document that you were shown a little earlier. This relates to an order for ten soldiers to hold the defence line at Podsjelovo. Is it right that, at point number 3, we can see here that you were assigned a squad commander to that group of ten men?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And still on this topic, and the final point, if we can please look at Exhibit 705.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Again, Mr. Sehic, this is a document that you were shown by the Prosecution only a short while ago. It relates to the attachment of men to the El Mujahid unit. It's right, isn't it, at point number B, you are clearly indicating there who is to be the commander of the men attached to the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, Mr. Sehic, I'd like to turn to another issue, and that is the issue of other Mujahedin fighters within the area. Would you agree with me that apart from the El Mujahedin Detachment, there were other Mujahedin groups operating in Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Do you know the locations of where any of those -- where the Mujahedin groups were based?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Some were deployed in the village called "Borovnica," i.e., Sehici,, where I was born. Some were born in the village of Imamovici and the surrounding villages. In any case, they were deployed in the general sector of Zavidovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: You've mentioned that they were in Imamovici. Whereabouts is Imamovici in relation to Borovnica, where you were based?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: To the northeast from Borovnica.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And are you able to say approximately how far away Imamovici is from Borovnica?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: About 20 kilometres or so.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And it's right to say, isn't it, that these groups were in the Ozren-Vozuca region around the time of the Vozuca action in September 1995?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Are you able to say when the group of Mujahedin arrived, approximately, in Borovnica?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: A somewhat larger group arrived maybe on the 8th or on the 9th September.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, in terms of the appearance of these Mujahedin fighters, could you tell us -- well, is it right to say that they dressed in a similar way to the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So some of them would wear military uniforms; is that so?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Would some of them also wear civilian clothing?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And would you agree with me that if you were to look at members of the Mujahedin based in Borovnica and compare them with a member of the El Mujahedin Detachment, you wouldn't be able to make a distinction between them? In other words, you wouldn't be able to tell, simply by appearance, which group they belonged to?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It would be difficult. Only some of those stayed in that village and they were referred to by the term "Kurds." They smoked and they did not look like Arabs. Some people said they were from Kurdistan, but I'm not sure. I can't confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Just to clarify that, did you say "Kurds," Mr. Sehic?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Rumours had it that there were 20 or more Kurds, and I personally saw them in the Vozuca sector. I was really astonished to see them smoking; whereas, Arabs almost never smoke. I don't remember ever having seen anybody from the El Mujahid unit smoking.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And, again, just to clarify the issue, apart from the Kurds that were in Borovnica, it's right that there were also Arabs based in that village who were similar in appearance to members of the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Okay. I want to turn to September 1995. You told us how, on the 10th of September, the attack was launched, and how the front lines moved. If I can take you to the 11th of September, you've explained how you received information that a large group of Serb soldiers had surrendered to the 2nd Company of your battalion; is that right?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: You also mentioned that orders had been issued by the 35th Division to the effect that all prisoners of war had to be taken to a collection point so that military police officers could take them over; is that right?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: You've told us that you believe the collection location was in Zavidovici, somewhere near the division command; is that so?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, you've explained that at a certain point, on the 11th of September, you yourself travelled to Kesten village, where you spoke to your deputy, Muhamed Omerasevic. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, were the Arabs, as you have called them, present in the village when you arrived at Kesten?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So you had the chance to see these Arabs for yourself. Is it correct that they had no insignia upon them to identify them as belonging to a particular group of Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: They did not have any insignia.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So would you agree with me that these Arabs that you saw there that day could have been members of any of the Mujahedin groups present in the Vozuca region at that time?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, your assistant commander for Security, Ismet Karahasanovic, made a list of all Serb detainees. Had he make the list after you arrived there, or did he make it after your arrival?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I believe that he had already made that list. I'm not sure that he included everybody on the list, but I should have thought so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Are you able to confirm that Mr. Karahasanovic had the identity cards and papers of the Serb soldiers with him when he prepared that list?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: He had some documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Do you recall did he take those documents away with him? Are you able to say?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: In your evidence, you've explained how the Arabs took the detainees away. As I understand your evidence, you yourself left Kesten, accompanied with two young boys.

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And you travelled to Krcevine on a route that took you through -- I beg your pardon. And you travelled to Marici village on a route that took you through Krcevine; is that right?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: As you travelled through Krcevine, you saw some men there that you think may have been the detained Serbs, but you're not able to say for sure; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Did you notice if there were Arabs with those men at the time?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: They were at a distance of some 50 metres or more. Their backs were turned to me, so I can't be sure, but I would have thought so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, I want to turn our attention to the list that was prepared by Mr. Karahasanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Perhaps if we could bring up the exhibit which shows the underlined portions made by Mr. Sehic, 695.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So, Mr. Sehic, is it correct that Mr. Karahasanovic gave you the list that he prepared in Kesten?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, not in Kesten, no. Some time later.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, you've explained to the Trial Chamber that you added certain phrases to the list prepared by Mr. Karahasanovic. You've told us that it was some time after. Are you able to say when you made these additions to this list?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I added some things ten or 15 days later, some other things after three or four months, and the last remarks were added maybe two or three years after the event. As I came by certain information, I added things on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So the information was added over a period of time, as long as maybe even three years after the list was prepared?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to ask you about what happened after you returned to Marici from Kesten. You told us that you gave a verbal report to your commander, Fuad Zilkic, around 1600 hours?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: You were also asked if you gave -- if there are any more discussions with the 328th Mountain Brigade about what happened in Kesten, and your response - and the reference to the transcript is page 31, line 21 - and what you said was: "In the days following that period, it was discussed as to what was going to happen to the soldiers of the 2nd Company, whether they would be rewarded or not."

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: You've explained to us that there were financial incentives in place for members of the ARBiH to capture enemy combatants. Would I be right -- would I be correct in saying that when you spoke to Commander Zilkic that day, and in the days that followed, your primary concern was about the financial situation relating to your men?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The soldiers and the officers of the 2nd Company that had carried out the task wanted explanation from me, whether they would be rewarded or not. It was only the money reward. Sometimes it was recognitions; sometimes it was commendations. So the commander of the 2nd Company should have been rewarded in writing, with a citation or something. But given the outcome of the whole situation, nobody was rewarded, nobody was promoted. There were no written citations issued or anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: If you'll just bear with me for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sehic, you met with Commander Zilkic that day, the 11th of September. The Prosecution showed you a document in the name of Fuad Zilkic, dated the 13th of September, and you were asked to comment upon that document. Would you agree with me that Commander Zilkic -- that you can't know what Commander Zilkic did with the information that you gave to him that day, if anything?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. He was my commander, and I was in no position, nor did I have to know, what he did with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions. Thank you, Mr. Sehic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Robson. Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No questions arising.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Sehic, when you got to Kesten and you saw these Serb soldiers being taken by the Arabs, did you know whether those Arabs were soldiers or not soldiers?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I didn't know. I assumed that they were soldiers, but I didn't expect civilians to be involved in such activities. That's how I assumed that they must have been soldiers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And did you have any idea what army they might have belonged to?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honour, I've already said earlier that it was exceptionally difficult to know which of the Arabs belonged to what units. We could not communicate with them. For the most part, they did not communicate either to the troops or to the officers of the army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, you said those Arabs outnumbered you. Do you remember saying that this morning?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, there's something that I don't understand, because you indicated that there were about a hundred 5th Battalion soldiers around Kesten on that day. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In the general area of Kesten, which included an area as far as five kilometres from the place where these things happened, on the road in the direction of Prokop, the terrain is quite rugged and the line of sight is impaired. The soldiers were close to that area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Now, forget about people who were five kilometres away. Right in Kesten, in the immediate vicinity of the capture, are you able to guesstimate how many of the 5th Battalion soldiers were there?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Around ten, at the most, judging from what I saw.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That explains my query. You also testified, when you were asked questions by the Prosecutor, that there were always orders that specified what should be done with captured persons and booty. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What did the order say should be done with these people and the booty?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The captured soldiers were to be treated in a military fashion. As per the Geneva Conventions, they were to be handed over to the military police of the 328th Brigade of the 35th Division, and that's what almost every order contained.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And at the time, you were aware of those instructions in the order?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And according to your observations, were these captured prisoners being treated according -- being handled according to the Geneva Conventions? You're saying your orders instructed you that they must be given over to the military police of the 328th Brigade. Was that what was happening at the time?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: For the most part, yes, and I believed that that group was going to be handed over to the military police, too. However, the problem was that they wanted to take the war booty for themselves. As for the other prisoners, including the two civilians and the two children, we always handed them over to the military police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, you were asked earlier a question by Judge Lattanzi as to what your major interest was at the time, and I think you had indicated that your major interest was the two children; right?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You're saying and do I understand it is your evidence that you were satisfied that the other prisoners that were taken away were being dealt with okay, and that's why they were not part of your concern? That they were being treated according to orders, that's your evidence?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. That clarifies my point. My last question to you is: You say, when you left Kesten, going to the village of Sehici [sic], past Krcevine, you saw these people who were plus/minus 50 metres away, and you believed that they were the captured soldiers?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: You mean the village of Marici, not Sehici?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Marici, I beg your pardon, Marici. You were going to Marici, but you were passing Krcevine?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I saw a group I was not sure was of those captured soldiers. I believe that they were, but I was not sure because they had their backs turned to me. I did not see their faces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You didn't recognise anything about them that you had seen when you were in Kesten? It was just a belief. Okay. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was in passing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: How strong was that belief?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Judge Harhoff has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Sehic, I just have one question relating to another observation you made in respect of the prisoners of war, and that relates to the three women that you testified were there also. I thought you said that the security officer had delivered them to the command post in Marici. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. He separated them from the men and sent them by courier toward the command post in the village of Marici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So these three women were not taken by the El Mujahid Detachment; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On the road toward Marici, the El Mujahid vehicle saw the escort accompanying these three women. They pulled over, and they took the three women away with them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I see. So the three women never reached the command post in Marici?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: How did you learn this?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The courier who was supposed to take them there came to me as I returned from the village of Marici, at around 1600 or 1700 hours, or rather, it was from Kesten that I returned, not from Marici, that the person who was tasked with escorting them there informed me about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: But the three women, I take it, were civilians, were they not?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Were they taken out of the group of prisoners of war before you arrived to Kesten? Is that why you did not see it.

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I didn't see them at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Did you inquire whether they were civilians?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. I inquired about that. One of them said that she had worked in the army kitchens. So she was in the army, and I don't know about the others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: What was your assessment of these three women being taken prisoners of war? Did you consider that a lawful, a legal action or not?

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I believed that they, too, would be exchanged. Later on, we received some information indicating that they had been exchanged, indeed, but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Well, sir, for them to be exchanged as prisoners of war, they would have had to be taken legitimately as prisoners, themselves. You can't take --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Obviously, you cannot take civilians and use them as devices to exchange. So if you were not sure that they were civilians or lawful combatants, I would have thought that you would have inquired about this and made sure that they were, indeed, combatants and not civilians, because if they had been civilians, they would have been unlawfully detained.

utterances.speaker: AHMET SEHIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The soldier who talked to them said that one of them admitted to having been in the Army of Republika Srpska; whereas, the other two did not admit that, although he believed that, indeed, all three were members of the army. I have to tell you again that I didn't see them at all. We expected that they would be handed over to the military police and that the military police would talk to them, or rather, that the security organs would act in keeping with the order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Any questions arising, Mr. Mundis?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Robson?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Robson. Sir, Mr. Sehic, that brings us to the conclusion of your testimony. Thank you very much for taking your time to come and testify at the Tribunal. You are now excused. You may stand down, and please travel well back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may stand down, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. That brings us to the conclusion of the proceedings for the day. We will postpone to Wednesday, the 7th, at quarter past 2.00, Courtroom II. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 7th day of November, 2007, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.44 p.m.,
